context: Super Saiyan 4 was designed by Tadayoshi Yamamuro, Dragon Ball's chief animation director. The form bypasses the gold-haired SSJ aesthetic for red fur and a Mohawk-style mane, returning to the Saiyans' Great Ape-tied roots. The form is non-canonical to Toriyama's later Dragon Ball Super continuity but remains beloved.

question: Tite Kubo's Bleach concluded its manga run in August 2016 after 686 chapters, with the final arc — the Thousand-Year Blood War — depicting the Soul Society's final war against an ancient race of Hollow-related humans called the Quincy. The Quincy King is an immortal being who's been waiting in a frozen state for centuries. What is his name?
choices: Aizen Sosuke, the original master deceiver
Kisuke Urahara, in his Quincy form revealed
context: Yhwach is the father of the Quincy race and a son of the Soul King himself. His power, 'The Almighty,' lets him see and rewrite the future. The Thousand-Year Blood War arc was animated in three cours from 2022 to 2024 — almost a decade after the manga concluded — by Studio Pierrot.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece reached a major narrative milestone in the Wano Country arc (2018-2022, manga chapters 909-1057), which concluded the long-running 'Pirates vs. Yonko' subplot by defeating two of the Four Emperors of the New World simultaneously. The arc also revealed the true name of Luffy's Devil Fruit, which had been called 'Gum-Gum Fruit' since chapter one but was actually a Mythical Zoan. What is the Fruit's true name?
answer: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika (the Human-Human Fruit, the Sun God form)
choices: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika (the Human-Human Fruit, the Sun God form)
Tori Tori no Mi, Model: Phoenix Sun (the Bird-Bird Fruit)
Mizu Mizu no Mi, Model: Liquid King (the Water-Water Fruit)
Hiya Hiya no Mi, Model: Solar Lord (the Sun-Sun Fruit)
context: The Nika reveal recontextualizes 1,000-plus chapters of the manga: Luffy is the reincarnation of a mythical 'Sun God of Liberation.' The reveal explains many of the franchise's earlier-arc mysteries (Joy Boy, the Will of D., the Void Century). Luffy's Gear 5 transformation — pure white with cartoonish rubber-physics absurdity — was the most-shared anime moment of 2023.

question: Aida Iro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun was animated by Lerche in early 2020 with director Masaomi Ando. The opening sequence used a distinctive paper-doll-cutout art style. The animation's color palette was an unusual choice for a horror-leaning supernatural series — heavy on what specific color tone?
answer: Soft pastel watercolors with chalk-blackboard accents
choices: Soft pastel watercolors with chalk-blackboard accents
Stark monochrome with neon-light highlight accents
Bright saturation with high-contrast comic-book inks
context: The series' distinctive look — chalk transitions, watercolor backgrounds, paper-cutout intro — set it apart from typical 2020s anime aesthetics. The opening sequence inspired countless TikTok and AMV recreations. Aida Iro's original manga art style is even more delicate; the anime adapted it with admirable fidelity.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto Shippuden arc 'Pain's Assault' (episodes 152-175) features the Akatsuki member Pain leveling the entire Hidden Leaf Village in a single attack. Pain's true identity is a young Akatsuki-founder named Nagato, who controls six bodies remotely as his 'Six Paths.' Nagato shares a tragic backstory with two childhood friends, including his teacher who later became one of the famous Three Legendary Ninja. Who was their teacher?
answer: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage and Pervy Sage from Naruto's backstory
choices: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage and Pervy Sage from Naruto's backstory
Orochimaru, the snake sannin and Sasuke's later mentor
Tsunade Senju, the slug sannin and Fifth Hokage
Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and original sensei
context: Jiraiya trained the war orphans Nagato, Yahiko, and Konan in the Rain Country. Yahiko's death drove Nagato to become Pain, the messianic Akatsuki founder. Jiraiya's death at Pain's hands in his investigative encounter is one of Shippuden's most devastating arcs. The reveal that Pain was Jiraiya's pupil mirrors Naruto's relationship with Jiraiya himself.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure has employed musical-name references for character and Stand names since Part 1 (1987). The infamous 'David Production anime curse' is the legal-clearance problem Araki's nomenclature creates. The Stand for Brando in Part 3 — 'The World' — is a reference to which musical entity?
answer: The 1987 album 'The World' by The Tygers of Pan Tang (later changed to 'Za Warudo' in some translations)
choices: The 1987 album 'The World' by The Tygers of Pan Tang (later changed to 'Za Warudo' in some translations)
The 1976 Frankie Valli single 'My Eyes Adored You' (renamed for licensing)
The 1981 song 'In the Air Tonight' by Phil Collins (similar musical motif)
The 1969 Beatles album cut 'Across the Universe' (extended track name)
context: Araki's musical references include over 300 character and Stand names taken from rock and metal artists. The David Production anime adaptation occasionally renamed Stands for international broadcast — 'Strawberry' became 'Wagon Wheel' in some markets, 'Sex Pistols' became 'Six Bullets,' etc. The original Japanese broadcasts kept the names intact.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter introduced the assassination-family of Killua Zoldyck — Gon's best friend and the franchise's iconic deuteragonist. The Zoldyck household lives on a private mountain estate called Kukuroo Mountain. The estate's outer gates are guarded by what specific creature, who must be 'tamed' by approaching family members?
answer: Mike, a massive guard hound trained to identify family bloodlines
choices: Mike, a massive guard hound trained to identify family bloodlines
Spike, an albino tiger captured from the Dark Continent
Zilch, a former Hunter Mafia chimera bound by a Manipulation Stand-equivalent
Click, a centuries-old phoenix trained by Zeno's grandfather
context: Mike's full name in the manga is 'Mike,' deliberately mundane against the elaborate Zoldyck family. He's the size of a small house and has eaten dozens of intruders. The Testing Gate at the entrance has six tonnage-weighted doors; Killua opens the third by default, the heaviest only opened by the patriarch Silva.

question: The original 1997 Pokemon anime's first season — known as the Indigo League — ran for 82 episodes, ending with Ash's appearance at the title League. Ash placed in the Top 16 in the league after a strong run was derailed by his Charizard's refusal to obey during a critical match. Which trainer beat Ash in that decisive Indigo League round?
answer: Ritchie, an Ash lookalike trainer with a Pikachu nicknamed Sparky
choices: Ritchie, an Ash lookalike trainer with a Pikachu nicknamed Sparky
Gary Oak, the Pallet Town rival, in a roundtable match
Gilbert, the Pewter Gym rematch trainer, in third round
Bruno, an Elite Four member, in an exhibition exception
context: Ritchie's appearance as a 'mirror Ash' character — same enthusiasm, same Pikachu, slightly more responsible — was a deliberate narrative beat. The Indigo League finale's lesson: Ash isn't ready to be a Pokemon Master yet. Ritchie himself loses in the next round, suggesting the same lesson applies broadly. The animator Masamitsu Hidaka cited the loss as character-defining.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball Z's Cell Saga concluded with the Cell Games — a martial-arts tournament Cell organizes to announce his perfect form to humanity. Goku, having trained alongside his son Gohan in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber, surprises everyone by stepping out of the final fight and pushing Gohan forward. Why does Goku withdraw?
answer: Goku has determined Gohan has greater untapped potential and a hidden form Cell hasn't seen
choices: Goku has determined Gohan has greater untapped potential and a hidden form Cell hasn't seen
Goku has secretly absorbed a fatal disease and saves his strength for the wish-revival
Goku has decided to die in the tournament to let Gohan inherit the family role of Earth's defender
Goku has been Saiyan-cursed by Vegeta's secret bargain and cannot win the fight
context: Gohan goes Super Saiyan 2 for the first time in the Cell Games after Cell crushes Android 16's last words. The transformation, animated by Mitsuo Hashimoto, became one of DBZ's most iconic moments. Gohan's Cell-decimating Kamehameha was set up by Goku from the other side; the father-son combo move is one of the franchise's most emotional sequences.

question: Studio Ghibli's Howl's Moving Castle (2004) was directed by Hayao Miyazaki and based on the 1986 Diana Wynne Jones novel. The film's English dub featured a notable A-list cast and a famously elegant fire-demon character voiced by what well-known American comedian?
answer: Billy Crystal, who improvised much of Calcifer's English-dub dialogue
choices: Billy Crystal, who improvised much of Calcifer's English-dub dialogue
Robin Williams, who voiced Howl's grandfather in the early scenes
Eddie Murphy, who provided the Witch of the Waste's voice
Dan Aykroyd, who took the King Sulliman role for the dub
context: The English dub also included Christian Bale (Howl), Emily Mortimer (young Sophie), Jean Simmons (old Sophie), and Lauren Bacall (Witch of the Waste). Calcifer is the fire-demon that powers Howl's moving castle through a contract that's secretly bound to Howl's heart. Disney distributed the dub through Miramax until that contract ended.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball franchise's recurring 'Hyperbolic Time Chamber' is a pocket dimension where one Earth-day equals one full year of training. The chamber sits inside Kami's Lookout, the floating palace at the top of Korin Tower. The chamber has specific entry restrictions: only two trainees at a time, and lifetime use limited per individual. What is the lifetime entry limit?
answer: Two cumulative days (two years of training) total per person across their lifetime
choices: Two cumulative days (two years of training) total per person across their lifetime
One cumulative day (one year of training) total per person across their lifetime
Three cumulative days (three years of training) total per person across their lifetime
One year of training maximum per individual entrance, no lifetime cap
context: The two-day lifetime rule is established early but interpreted loosely later in the series. The chamber's environment — 50x Earth gravity, harsh temperature extremes, no horizon — makes survival difficult. The chamber was destroyed by Super Buu in the Buu arc, eliminating the franchise's deus-ex-machina training tool for later arcs.

question: In Naruto Shippuden, the major character death that traumatized the fanbase most in the war arc was a sage-cloaked, fox-summoning ninja master killed by Pain in his investigative encounter. The death scene featured the master writing his final findings on his opponent's back in coded text as his last act. Name the master.
answer: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage of Mt. Myoboku
choices: Jiraiya, the Toad Sage of Mt. Myoboku
Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage Professor
context: Jiraiya wrote 'The real Pain' (and partial body locations) on his pursuer Fukasaku's back before dying in the Hidden Rain village. Pain — actually his student Nagato's six-corpse-puppet — defeated him in close combat using a body that hadn't been revealed. Jiraiya's death is widely cited as one of shonen's most-emotional sequences. His sacrifice cracks the Pain mystery for Konoha.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has an iconic chapter where Light realizes L is in the same room as him for the first time. The two have been monitoring each other's behavior for weeks. The scene that confirms their suspicions involves Light, L, and a specific clandestine activity at L's hotel suite. What is the activity?
answer: A televised tennis match Light watches while L watches him watching
choices: A televised tennis match Light watches while L watches him watching
An informal chess game between Light and Soichiro Yagami at L's invitation
A car ride from To-Oh to Light's home with Watari at the wheel
A surveillance-camera review with Light helping L with the case
context: The tennis sequence is famously voiced in inner monologue, with both Light and L providing first-person commentary on what they're observing about the other. Obata's drawing style on this sequence — close-ups of eyes, the ball, the racket — became defining for the manga's psychological-thriller register. The eventual face-to-face came at the To-Oh entrance ceremony.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece's Marineford War arc featured the death of the World's Strongest Man Edward Newgate — alias Whitebeard — during his attempt to rescue Luffy's brother Ace from public execution. Whitebeard's final death pose was a famously dramatic standing-corpse moment with both arms folded. His final words named his successor and addressed Blackbeard. What did he announce about Joy Boy and the One Piece?
answer: He confirmed One Piece exists, that Joy Boy is the prophesied figure, and that one day his successor would inherit his ambitions
choices: He confirmed One Piece exists, that Joy Boy is the prophesied figure, and that one day his successor would inherit his ambitions
He warned Blackbeard's crew that the Devil Fruit transfer would cost them their lives within five years
He apologized to his fallen division-commander sons and named Marco as the next Whitebeard captain
He confessed that the Ancient Weapons were all held by Eldian descendants of an erased kingdom
context: Whitebeard's standing-death scene shocked One Piece readers when it was first published in 2010. His final words — 'The One Piece does exist!' — were the single biggest plot confirmation in over a decade of the manga. Blackbeard's subsequent body-double-Devil-Fruit acquisition created a one-of-a-kind exception to the franchise's power rules. Marco the Phoenix took over leadership of Whitebeard's remnants.

question: Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia features a recurring battle structure involving 'Pillar' heroes, the franchise's tier above standard Pro Heroes. The series's number-two hero — Endeavor — is the Pillar hero who covers western Japan. His son Shoto Todoroki famously refused to use the inherited fire-side of his quirk for years. What pulled Shoto out of that refusal?
answer: Deku's heart-to-heart with him during their Sports Festival fight
choices: Deku's heart-to-heart with him during their Sports Festival fight
His mother Rei's hospital recovery and explicit forgiveness offered
Endeavor's near-death battle against the high-end Nomu years later
Iida's brother Tensei being assaulted by Stain in a related arc
context: The Sports Festival arc semi-final fight between Deku and Todoroki is one of MHA's defining episodes. Deku — bleeding, broken, and using One For All at minimum percent — convinced Todoroki that his fire was 'his own, not his father's.' The scene cemented Horikoshi's reputation for combining shonen fights with character development. Todoroki's reconciliation with his family unfolds over the manga's last 100 chapters.

question: In Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia, Class 1-A homeroom teacher Shota Aizawa (Eraserhead) carries a signature item that lets him bind and restrain enemies while his quirk-canceling gaze cuts off their powers. What's the item?
answer: His capture weapon — a binding scarf of steel-wire-cored cloth
choices: His capture weapon — a binding scarf of steel-wire-cored cloth
A pair of armored gauntlets — with retractable wire-launchers in each palm
A monofilament whip — coiled around his belt and weighted at the tip
A modified bullwhip — braided from carbon-aramid fiber with handle grips
context: Aizawa's quirk Erasure cancels other quirks while he keeps eye contact, and his dry eyes force him to blink — limiting how long he can use it. His capture weapon (officially called sōki bōgu / 'binding equipment' in the manga, often translated as 'capture weapon' or 'binding scarf') gives him a physical fighter's option during the seconds between quirk-cancels. The scarf trails from his neck like a scarf at rest, then articulates under his control during combat.

question: Hajime no Ippo's most famous training-arc image — the AC-current-jump-rope-with-pull-up-bar combination Takamura performs in his beach training — was reportedly modeled after a real-world strength regimen of a 1980s Japanese kickboxer. Morikawa Jouji visited multiple gyms researching the manga in the late 1980s. The actual gym whose roster of fighters Morikawa cited most heavily as his Kamogawa Boxing Gym template was located where?
answer: Sotomei-Yotsuya Boxing Gym in Tokyo, run by retired champion Eiji Sakurai during the 1980s
choices: Sotomei-Yotsuya Boxing Gym in Tokyo, run by retired champion Eiji Sakurai during the 1980s
Yokohama Tokai Boxing Gym, run by former Pacific champion Mitsuo Tanaka in the 1970s
Osaka Naniwa Boxing Club, run by world featherweight contender Hideo Yamamoto
Nagoya Kamogawa Gym, the actual real-world namesake of the manga's gym name
context: Morikawa Jouji's research methodology for Hajime no Ippo became famous in the industry. He interviewed dozens of active and retired professional boxers, trained at multiple gyms personally, and consulted on every fight choreography with real coaches. The Sotomei-Yotsuya influence is documented in his published author's notes. Coach Kamogawa was loosely modeled on multiple real-life gym owners, with Sakurai-style discipline blended in.

question: Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer was animated by Ufotable studio, who developed a distinctive digital-effects technique to handle the breathing-style attacks visually. Each breathing style — Water, Flame, Thunder — has its own signature color palette and animation feel. The water-style attacks famously look like they're being rendered as actual flowing water rather than illustrated effects. What 3D-to-2D production technique did Ufotable use for these sequences?
answer: A custom CGI-and-2D blend called digital chiaroscuro shading, with hand-painted Japanese-watercolor overlays
choices: A custom CGI-and-2D blend called digital chiaroscuro shading, with hand-painted Japanese-watercolor overlays
Pure 2D animation done frame-by-frame, with no CGI assistance whatsoever
Toon-shaded CGI exclusively, with no traditional cels at any production stage
Stop-motion-style sequencing combined with photographed live-action water elements
context: Ufotable's animation pipeline became industry-influential after Demon Slayer's success. The studio combines hand-painted backgrounds and character cels with carefully-calibrated CGI for the dynamic-effect sequences. The Mugen Train film's effect-animation work won multiple Japanese animation awards. The 'digital chiaroscuro' technique was originally developed for their Fate/Zero adaptation in 2011.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga used a recurring narrative device — chakra-mark sealing — that has roots in real Japanese folk-religious tradition. The 'Dragon Sealing Method' Jiraiya uses to bind the Nine-Tailed Fox into baby Naruto draws from a real-world ritualistic talisman class associated with which Shinto temple complex?
answer: Mount Koya's esoteric Buddhist-Shinto syncretic tradition, with mountain-ascetic Tendai influences
choices: Mount Koya's esoteric Buddhist-Shinto syncretic tradition, with mountain-ascetic Tendai influences
Ise Grand Shrine's purely Shinto purification-rite documentation
Nikko Toshogu's elaborate Tokugawa-era warding talisman archive
context: Kishimoto did extensive Buddhist-Shinto research during Naruto's serialization. The Sealing Jutsu vocabulary borrows from Mikkyo (esoteric Buddhism) ritual language. The 'Five Element' chakra system (Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Lightning) corresponds to the Godai cosmology shared between Shinto and Buddhist traditions. The Jinchuriki concept — humans imprisoning gods — has loose parallels to real-world Inari fox-spirit lore.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece set a Guinness World Record in 2022 for the most copies published of a single comic book series by an individual author — over 516 million copies worldwide. The previous record-holder for most-published-by-single-author was Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball. Oda has stated his original plan for the series finale (drafted in 1997 before he began serialization) involves a specific number of chapters. Roughly how many chapters did Oda originally tell his editor One Piece would last?
answer: About five years' worth — Oda originally planned roughly 250 chapters total
choices: About five years' worth — Oda originally planned roughly 250 chapters total
About ten years' worth — Oda planned roughly 500 chapters total
About fifteen years' worth — Oda planned roughly 750 chapters total
About twenty years' worth — Oda planned roughly 1,000 chapters total
context: Oda is famously documented as believing he would finish the series quickly. As of 2026, One Piece has crossed 1,100 chapters and is in its final saga. Oda's continued recommitment to the original ending — 'I'll never deviate from what I planned' — has become a fan running joke. The series has been the best-selling manga of every single year from 2008 through the present.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan reached its serialization conclusion in April 2021 after 139 chapters across 12 years. The final chapter's title was a specific Japanese phrase meaning 'Toward the Tree on That Hill' — a callback to the manga's opening dream-sequence in chapter one. The English translation localized the title significantly. What did the official English release title the final chapter?
answer: Toward the Tree on That Hill
choices: Toward the Tree on That Hill
A Long Dream by the Sea
The Last Boy in the World
context: The chapter title's callback to chapter one is one of the manga's signature framing devices. Isayama planted the chapter-one dream sequence as a deliberate beat designed to be revisited in the finale. The fan reaction to the actual final chapter was mixed — some celebrated the bookended structure, others felt the ending was rushed. The 4-page extended ending released several months later softened the controversy.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has an iconic recurring object: the Death Note itself, with a black leather cover and English-language inscription. The notebook's rules — 'The human whose name is written in this notebook shall die' — are introduced in the cold open of chapter one. Obata's drawing of the actual physical notebook went through several design iterations. The final notebook design was based on what specific real-world object Ohba and Obata used as reference?
answer: A Moleskine-style notebook with custom hand-cut leather cover provided by Shueisha's production team
choices: A Moleskine-style notebook with custom hand-cut leather cover provided by Shueisha's production team
A Hong Kong-import calligraphy notebook with traditional Chinese binding
A vintage 1940s Italian notebook from the publisher's reference archives
A standard Japanese school-supply composition book modified by the author
context: Obata reportedly had Shueisha's production team prepare a hand-tooled leather notebook as the visual reference. The cover's grain texture, the binding stitch, and the page-edging were all carefully reproduced in Obata's panels. The English-language 'Death Note' lettering on the cover became one of the manga's most iconic visual elements. The 2017 Netflix adaptation's prop notebook was also custom-made to Obata's design.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist features Edward Elric's signature transmutation circle — a hand-clapping fast-circle technique he developed after seeing the Gate of Truth. The hand-clap is a faster alternative to drawing a circle on the ground or having one tattooed on the palms. The technique is uncommon in alchemists — fewer than ten in the entire series achieve it without seeing the Gate first. What gave Ed the ability to skip the formal circle?
answer: He had seen the Gate of Truth and 'paid the toll' for human transmutation knowledge
choices: He had seen the Gate of Truth and 'paid the toll' for human transmutation knowledge
His father Hohenheim's Philosopher's-Stone-blood lineage gave him innate transmutation access
His mentor Izumi Curtis taught him a secret hand-clap technique she'd kept private
His prosthetic automail arm contained a built-in transmutation array invented by Winry
context: The 'paid the toll' framework is FMA's central magic-system principle: every alchemist who exceeds normal rules has seen the Gate. Other circle-less alchemists include Alphonse (also paid the toll for the failed transmutation), Izumi Curtis (paid for losing her ability to bear children), and the homunculus Father (who is essentially a transmutation circle made flesh). The 'hand-clap' technique became one of the manga's most-imitated visual signatures.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter has been famous for the author's frequent hiatuses — Togashi's chronic back pain has interrupted serialization repeatedly since 1998. The longest single continuous hiatus in the manga's run was a multi-year break that lasted from 2018 to 2022. During that hiatus, Shueisha continued to publish status updates from Togashi on his Twitter account documenting his slow page-by-page progress. Roughly how many pages did Togashi complete during the four-year hiatus before serialization resumed?
answer: About 95 pages — released as 10 chapters in October 2022
choices: About 95 pages — released as 10 chapters in October 2022
About 30 pages — released as 4 chapters in mid-2022
About 200 pages — saved for a full-volume publication
About 60 pages — held for an as-yet-unreleased volume 38
context: Togashi's October 2022 return chapter was the manga's first new content since November 2018. The 10-chapter burst was Volume 37, focused on the Dark Continent expedition arc. Togashi's published explanations cite a herniated disc and chronic lower-back problems that prevent him from drawing at a manga-rate page schedule. His wife Naoko Takeuchi (creator of Sailor Moon) has reportedly assisted with some assistance-tasks during his recovery.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure has gone through 9 Parts over its 38-year run. Araki's distinctive art style — exaggerated muscle anatomy, theatrical posing, fashion-magazine influences — has evolved dramatically across the Parts. Araki has stated in interviews that his major art-style influences were two specific visual-art traditions: Italian Renaissance fresco-painting and what specific Western fashion-magazine genre?
answer: Italian high-fashion photography of the 1960s through 1980s, especially Versace campaigns
choices: Italian high-fashion photography of the 1960s through 1980s, especially Versace campaigns
French haute-couture sketches of the 1950s, especially Dior and Balmain runway documentation
American Vogue editorial spreads of the 1970s, especially Diana Vreeland-era cover work
British rock-magazine cover photography of the 1980s, especially NME and Smash Hits
context: The Versace-and-Renaissance synthesis is one of JoJo's defining aesthetic principles. Araki has repeatedly cited Gianni Versace as a personal inspiration; the manga's character designs often reference specific Versace runway looks. Araki himself appears in the manga periodically as a self-portrait character drawn in his typical Italian-fashion-art style. His 2018 art exhibition at the Louvre paired his work with Renaissance pieces.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Yu Yu Hakusho concluded in 1994 with the Three Kings arc — a shortened version of his original plan. Togashi had originally pitched Yu Yu Hakusho to Weekly Shonen Jump as a much darker, more political series with a different protagonist concept than the eventual Yusuke. The original pitch (rejected by editors) starred what kind of character?
answer: A reincarnated war veteran returned to life as a yakuza fighter, drawn in a noir style
choices: A reincarnated war veteran returned to life as a yakuza fighter, drawn in a noir style
A small-town teacher haunted by school-bullying ghosts in a horror style
A modern-day samurai detective investigating supernatural crimes in Edo style
An esports-prodigy schoolboy fighting demons in a video-game-rules style
context: Togashi has discussed in retrospectives that Yu Yu Hakusho's eventual shonen-action shape was significantly reworked from his original noir-influenced pitch. The shonen restructure required keeping the supernatural-detective premise but adding a teenage protagonist, a romantic subplot, and tournament arcs. Yusuke Urameshi as a redeemed-delinquent character was the editor's compromise structure. Togashi cited the experience as a factor in his later Hunter x Hunter approach.

question: Shuichi Shigeno's Initial D's Eurobeat-soundtrack identity is built around a specific recording label called Avex Trax, whose 'Super Eurobeat' compilation series ran from 1990 to 2014 with 250 volumes. The earliest Initial D soundtrack used what the franchise considered 'the' definitive Eurobeat artist — a single Italian musician credited with the genre's iconic high-BPM driving feel. What was this artist's stage name?
answer: Dave Rodgers, whose tracks like 'Deja Vu' and 'Speedy Speed Boy' became Initial D staples
choices: Dave Rodgers, whose tracks like 'Deja Vu' and 'Speedy Speed Boy' became Initial D staples
Max Coveri, whose tracks like 'Running in the 90s' became Initial D staples
Manuel Tognella, whose tracks like 'Driving Spirit' became Initial D staples
Mickey B, whose tracks like the wartime-coded title cut became Initial D staples
context: Dave Rodgers (born Giancarlo Pasquini in Italy, 1963) is widely credited as the Eurobeat genre's most iconic figure. His tracks were licensed extensively by Avex Trax for Initial D's soundtrack across the 1990s and early 2000s. 'Deja Vu' specifically — the iconic 'Akina Downhill' theme — became one of the most-recognized anime music tracks of all time, with billions of YouTube plays.

question: Studio Ghibli's Princess Mononoke (1997) included a famously controversial demon-boar opening sequence. The demon-boar Nago — corrupted by an iron-ball wound inflicted by Lady Eboshi's iron-mining operation — attacks the protagonist's village in the film's first scene. The detailed corruption-tentacle CGI used to render the demon-boar was Studio Ghibli's first significant use of computer-generated imagery. About what percentage of the film involved CGI work?
answer: About 10 percent of total shots, mostly in the demon-corruption and forest-spirit sequences
choices: About 10 percent of total shots, mostly in the demon-corruption and forest-spirit sequences
About 30 percent of total shots, throughout the film for textures and crowd scenes
About 1 percent of total shots, restricted to a single establishing-shot sky
About 50 percent of total shots, in an unprecedented CGI integration for Ghibli
context: Ghibli's CGI use grew gradually from Princess Mononoke through the 2000s. Spirited Away's bathhouse sequences used CGI for set extension and crowd work. Howl's Moving Castle used CGI for the castle's mechanical animations. Miyazaki's approach has consistently been to use CGI only where traditional cel animation would be impractical or impossible. The Princess Mononoke demon-corruption tentacles set the studio's CGI-aesthetic standard.

question: Aida Iro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun introduces the manga's deeper plot in a specific extended arc called the Mokke Arc — featuring the small, mochi-shaped Mokke spirits who supply 'spiritual mochi' as currency between the Seven Mysteries. The Mokke trade in a specific commodity rumored to grant wishes. What do the Mokke trade?
answer: Konpeito, traditional Japanese sugar-candy-stars, traded as spiritual currency
choices: Konpeito, traditional Japanese sugar-candy-stars, traded as spiritual currency
Mochi-rice cakes, blessed by the Mokke clan's matriarch
Ningyo-yaki, traditional doll-shaped pancakes filled with bean paste
Wagashi, traditional seasonal sweets made for tea ceremony
context: Konpeito (also spelled konpeitō) is the small star-shaped sugar candy of Japanese tradition, originally brought to Japan by 16th-century Portuguese traders. Aida Iro uses the candy as Hanako-kun's currency-of-the-supernatural with deliberate cultural-resonance. Konpeito are central to several arcs in the manga, including the resolution of the Mirror Mystery storyline. The Mokke themselves are tiny, mostly-cute creatures who serve as the manga's comic relief.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note has a famous chapter — Chapter 58 — where Light realizes L is recording everything. The chapter's dramatic reveal hinges on a recurring camera-detection device introduced earlier. Light's mind narrates a Plan A through F sequence aloud as he calculates the moves. Of the six lettered plans, which was the actual one Light executed?
answer: Plan B, the contingency that involved a specific date-marked notebook-page
choices: Plan B, the contingency that involved a specific date-marked notebook-page
Plan A, the primary intended approach with no contingency
Plan E, the doomsday option with a Watari-targeting clause
Plan F, the only one Light actually rehearsed in advance
context: Chapter 58 of the manga is widely cited as one of Death Note's tightest-written sequences. Light's internal monologue — listing six lettered plans, executing the contingency, and silently saying 'just as planned' — was animated by Madhouse in the 2006 anime with iconic effect. The 'just as planned' moment became one of anime's most-quoted phrases, alongside 'I'll take a potato chip... AND EAT IT.'

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball Z's Trunks arc (1991-1993) introduced a future timeline where Goku has died of a heart virus and the Androids 17 and 18 have killed all the Z fighters. The arc's centerpiece is the visit of teenaged future Trunks from that timeline, traveling back to warn the present-day Z fighters. Trunks gives Goku a specific medicine to take when he develops the same heart virus. What is the medicine?
answer: A specific anti-heart-virus pharmaceutical from the future, in a Capsule Corp medicine bottle
choices: A specific anti-heart-virus pharmaceutical from the future, in a Capsule Corp medicine bottle
A sample of Dr. Gero's android-engineering blueprints in microfilm format
A Saiyan-bloodline immunity injection developed by Bulma's lab in the future
A serum from a senzu-bean cross-bred with synthetic immune-system tissue
context: The future-Trunks visit kicks off the Cell Saga; Trunks is the son of Bulma and Vegeta in a future where Goku died and the Z fighters were destroyed. Toriyama's careful work to keep both timelines coherent (the future Trunks's birth, the present-day Trunks's birth, the medicine plot point) became a model for shonen time-travel structures. Trunks's red Capsule Corp jacket and his sword (passed down from Tapion in the films) became iconic franchise looks.

question: Tite Kubo's Bleach features a recurring 'zanpakuto release' command structure: each Soul Reaper's sealed sword has a unique release command-phrase that activates its Shikai form. Captain Toshiro Hitsugaya's command 'Souten ni Zase, Hyorinmaru!' translates loosely to 'Reign over the frozen heavens, Hyorinmaru!' His released zanpakuto becomes a long-bladed ice-dragon-themed sword. Hitsugaya is which Squad's captain?
choices: Squad 13, the Western Rukongai recruitment-and-protection squad
Squad 6, the noble Kuchiki-family squad of intellectual warriors
Squad 4, the medical and recovery squad led by Unohana
context: Hitsugaya is the youngest captain in the Gotei 13, having attained his rank as a child prodigy. His Bankai, Daiguren Hyorinmaru, is one of the most-rendered shows of bankai in the anime. The character's design — short, silver-haired, with a perpetually-scowling face — made him a fan favorite immediately. His relationship with his squad's lieutenant Rangiku Matsumoto is one of Bleach's most-loved character pairings.

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece introduced Wano Country in chapter 909 and used the arc to officially confirm the long-rumored 'Joy Boy' legend from the Void Century. The Void Century is a roughly-100-year period of erased history about 800 years before the present, when an ancient kingdom was destroyed by an alliance of 19 other kingdoms — the ancestors of the present-day World Government. What is the erased ancient kingdom called?
answer: The Great Kingdom (the Ancient Kingdom of D., never given a public name in-canon)
choices: The Great Kingdom (the Ancient Kingdom of D., never given a public name in-canon)
The Kingdom of Lulusia, the central island-nation of the One Piece world
The Holy Kingdom of God Valley, where the original Celestial Dragons originated
The Atlantean Crown, the underwater nation Joy Boy's people ruled
context: The Great Kingdom's destruction is the foundational event of One Piece's worldbuilding. The 'Will of D.' inheritance system (Luffy's middle name, Roger's middle name, Blackbeard's middle name) is a remnant of the lost kingdom's bloodline. The Marines and World Government have suppressed all knowledge of the kingdom's name and history for 800 years. The truth of the Void Century is set to be revealed in One Piece's final saga.

question: Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer has a famous Easter-egg moment in the manga's final chapter: a modern-day Tokyo epilogue showing the reincarnations of the main cast as ordinary high-schoolers about a century later. The epilogue depicts what was supposed to be the cast's 'happy ending in another life.' One specific reincarnation is shown reading a book at a cafe. Which character's reincarnation is reading?
answer: Kanao Tsuyuri's reincarnation, reading a romance novel at a Tokyo cafe
choices: Kanao Tsuyuri's reincarnation, reading a romance novel at a Tokyo cafe
Tanjiro's reincarnation, reading a children's storybook on a train
Kanroji Mitsuri's reincarnation, reading a Greek mythology textbook
Zenitsu's reincarnation, reading a music magazine in the school library
context: The modern-Tokyo epilogue runs from chapters 200 to 205 of the manga. The reincarnations are mostly cousins or descendants of the original cast, with a few exceptions (Kanao herself appears slightly older). The manga's final beat is a quiet, peaceful Tokyo scene contrasting against the demon-fighting violence of the main story. Gotouge was clear in interviews that this 100-years-later setting was intentional.

question: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto's final arc — the Shinobi World War (episodes 261-479 in Shippuden) — features the Akatsuki-and-Madara reanimation of the previous generation of dead ninja using a forbidden jutsu. The technique, called Edo Tensei (Impure World Reincarnation), was developed by a specific previous Hokage who later became known as a war criminal. Which Hokage created the technique?
answer: The Second Hokage Tobirama Senju, brother and successor to Hashirama
choices: The Second Hokage Tobirama Senju, brother and successor to Hashirama
The First Hokage Hashirama Senju, the founder of the village
The Third Hokage Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Professor of Konoha
The Fourth Hokage Minato Namikaze, the Yellow Flash
context: Tobirama created Edo Tensei to bind the dead to living-tissue vessels — the technique is universally banned, but Orochimaru and Madara revive it for war purposes. The reanimated ninja include the previous four Hokage, Itachi, the Akatsuki, and dozens of others. The reanimation scenes were the manga's longest and most spectacle-driven sequences. Tobirama's status as inventor of multiple forbidden jutsu (including Edo Tensei and the original Flying Thunder God) became defining.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan features a recurring symbol — a pair of crossed wings — that represents the Survey Corps regiment. The original wing-emblem design has cultural-symbolic roots in real-world Western military tradition. Isayama has cited a specific historical military regiment as direct inspiration. What regiment was the source of the Wings of Freedom design?
answer: The British Royal Air Force's Pathfinder squadron of WWII
choices: The British Royal Air Force's Pathfinder squadron of WWII
The Imperial Japanese Army's Tokkotai (Special Attack Unit) of WWII
The German Luftwaffe's Schnellbomber squadron of the early Battle of Britain
The Soviet Union's Yak-9 aerial-superiority wing of the Eastern Front
context: Isayama studied multiple Western military traditions for AOT's visual design. The Survey Corps's crossed-wings emblem, the boot-and-trouser uniform style, and the cavalry-rank organization all draw from real WWII-era European militaries. The German-language naming convention for characters (Eren, Mikasa, Armin, etc.) similarly draws from Isayama's research. The Pathfinder squadron's role — finding enemy territory in the dark — fits the Survey Corps's narrative function.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 5 — Vento Aureo / Golden Wind — is set in Italy in 2001 and follows the young mafia recruit Giorno Giovanna. Giorno is the son of a character from a previous part — specifically, the son of the original immortal vampire from Part 1, conceived during one of his stolen-body episodes. Which Joestar-or-Joestar-adjacent character is Giorno's mother?
answer: Yuhko, a Japanese woman impregnated by the vampire while he wore Jonathan Joestar's stolen body in 1989
choices: Yuhko, a Japanese woman impregnated by the vampire while he wore Jonathan Joestar's stolen body in 1989
Erina Pendleton, Jonathan's widow returned for a brief Italian vacation
Tonpetty's daughter, a Wamuu-Pillar-Man bloodline character
Caesar Zeppeli's mother, returned mysteriously after Part 2's events
context: The Giorno-paternity reveal is one of JoJo's signature lore details. Giorno inherits the Joestar bloodline through his father (the vampire who wore Jonathan's body) and the JoJo family of Stand users through his Joestar inheritance. His blond hair, golden eyes, and his Stand (Gold Experience) all reference his particular dual-bloodline status. Part 5 is set in Naples, Italy, and is heavily influenced by Italian fashion-and-film aesthetics.

question: Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note features a recurring secondary protagonist after L's death — the L-successor Near (real name Nate River). Near is depicted as a young albino child who plays with toys and dice while solving cases. Near's introduction in the manga's second arc featured a specific physical gesture that became one of his signature visual elements. What does Near constantly do while thinking?
answer: He twists a single lock of his white hair around his index finger
choices: He twists a single lock of his white hair around his index finger
He arranges a chess match between miniature figures on a desk
He cracks his knuckles in a specific six-finger pattern
He counts dice and arranges them in pyramidal stacks on the floor
context: Near's hair-twisting habit is one of the manga's most-replicated character tics. Obata's drawings show the gesture frequently — close-ups of the finger in the curl of white hair became standard Near framing. The character is meant to be even more reclusive than L, with anxieties about social contact. Near's eventual confrontation with Light, ending the manga's main arc, is structured as a deliberate parallel-mirror to L's earlier confrontation.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood (2009-2010) was the second TV anime adaptation of her manga, replacing the 2003 anime's diverging plot with a faithful-to-the-source adaptation. The Brotherhood adaptation's opening theme — a song called 'Again' — was performed by what Japanese rock band?
answer: Yui (a solo artist, not a band), whose 'Again' opens Brotherhood's first arc
choices: Yui (a solo artist, not a band), whose 'Again' opens Brotherhood's first arc
Asian Kung-Fu Generation, whose 'Rewrite' opened the 2003 series instead
The High Wide and Handsome, an indie group used for opening rotations
L'Arc-en-Ciel, whose 'My Heart Draws a Dream' was used for Episode 50
context: Yui's 'Again' became one of the most-recognized anime opening themes of the late 2000s. Her solo work was characterized by acoustic guitar-driven J-rock with strong vocal melodies. The Brotherhood adaptation by Studio Bones is widely considered the better adaptation of the manga, with five different opening themes across its run. Asian Kung-Fu Generation's 'Rewrite' is iconic but belongs to the 2003 series.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball franchise's iconic Saiyan-arc transformation 'Super Saiyan' (later distinguished as the 'first transformation' in the franchise's hierarchy) requires the user to be a Saiyan and to reach an emotional breaking point of intense rage. The original concept for Super Saiyan came to Toriyama during the Frieza fight; his editor at the time was named Kazuhiko Torishima. What was Torishima's reaction when Toriyama proposed Goku's transformation?
answer: Torishima loved it and reportedly told Toriyama 'this is the breakthrough'
choices: Torishima loved it and reportedly told Toriyama 'this is the breakthrough'
Torishima resisted, calling the idea derivative of Berserk's behavior shift
Torishima requested major design changes including different hair color
Torishima initially rejected the idea, suggesting a power-up sword instead
context: Toriyama and Torishima had a famously productive working relationship. The Super Saiyan design — gold hair, teal eyes, glowing aura — emerged from Toriyama's own preference for high-contrast color palettes and was approved with minimal editorial intervention. The transformation became one of anime's most-imitated tropes, with countless other shonen series featuring similar 'breakthrough power-up' sequences. The Saiyan-rage trigger remained part of the franchise's core canon through Dragon Ball Super.

question: Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball Z's Buu Saga concluded with a final Spirit Bomb attack against the universe's most powerful demon (Kid Buu). The Spirit Bomb required energy donations from every living being on Earth. Hercule (Mr. Satan) — the boastful champion who'd been masquerading as Cell's killer — was the one who successfully convinced humanity to raise their hands and donate energy. The character was Toriyama's deliberate satire of what kind of figure?
answer: A bombastic Western pro wrestler, with a name riffing on Hulk Hogan
choices: A bombastic Western pro wrestler, with a name riffing on Hulk Hogan
A Japanese sumo grand champion (yokozuna), of late-1980s celebrity status
A 1980s American bodybuilding magazine cover star, in the Lou Ferrigno mold
An Italian motorcycle daredevil of the Evel Knievel tradition
context: The Hercule / Mr. Satan name choice was a deliberate Toriyama joke. The character's hairstyle, his boastful interview style, his merchandising-heavy fame — all reference the pro-wrestling celebrity culture of the late 1980s. Hercule's redemption arc in the Buu Saga — convincing humanity to save Goku, befriending Majin Buu — turned what was a comic-relief satire into one of the franchise's most-loved characters. The dub's name 'Hercule' was a licensing-driven change from his Japanese 'Mr. Satan.'

question: Eiichiro Oda's One Piece introduced the Pirate King concept in chapter one with the words of the executed Pirate King Gol D. Roger: 'My treasure? If you want it, it's yours. I left everything I had in One Piece.' These were the public final words spoken by Roger on the execution platform at Loguetown. The execution started 22 years before Luffy's chapter-one departure. Roger's final words and their public broadcast kicked off what's referred to in the franchise as what era?
choices: The Golden Age of the Sea
context: The Great Pirate Era is the active framing the World Government uses for the post-Roger period. Twenty-two years of pirate activity were directly enabled by Roger's final words; the four Yonko (Whitebeard, Big Mom, Kaido, and later Blackbeard) are the present-day equivalents of the older 'Rocks Pirates.' One Piece's narrative tension between law-and-pirate-freedom is the foundational genre-mechanic of the entire manga. Luffy's stated goal — to find One Piece and become King of the Pirates — directly continues Roger's announced legacy.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter introduced the Hunter Examination arc — a multi-stage qualification test that turns ordinary applicants into licensed Hunters of the international Hunter Association. The exam's final stage is a one-on-one combat tournament where each examiner fights one specific applicant. The exam's chair examiner during the year-one arc is which character?
answer: Netero, the chairman of the Hunter Association
choices: Netero, the chairman of the Hunter Association
Hisoka, the freelance examiner who'd taken the test years prior
Bisuke (Biscuit Krueger), in disguise as a child examiner
Kurapika, who's actually a fellow applicant taking it for the first time
context: Netero himself organized and oversaw the year-one Hunter Exam in which Gon, Killua, Kurapika, and Leorio participated. His chairmanship would later become important in the Chimera Ant arc when he personally challenges Meruem. The Hunter Exam is a recurring narrative device in the franchise; it's been remade in five different forms across Togashi's various story arcs. The Hunter Association's secret 'Zodiacs' inner circle is one of HxH's most-imitated worldbuilding elements.

question: In the original 1997 Pokemon anime, Ash Ketchum was given Pikachu as his starter at Professor Oak's lab because all three of the regional starters had already been given out by the time Ash overslept on his tenth birthday. The animation team made an unprecedented choice for the anime: ignoring the Pokemon Red/Blue games' starter trio and making the marketing-friendly electric mouse the protagonist's partner. Who specifically advocated within the production team to make Pikachu the starter?
answer: Producer Takemoto Mori at Shogakukan, citing Pikachu's plush-toy potential and child-recognition data
choices: Producer Takemoto Mori at Shogakukan, citing Pikachu's plush-toy potential and child-recognition data
Series director Junichi Masuda, in disagreement with Satoshi Tajiri who'd preferred Bulbasaur
Animator Sayuri Ichiishi, who'd designed the Pikachu's anime-specific facial expressions
Marketing executive Junichi Nishioka, who'd run focus groups on the original Red/Blue cover art
context: The Pikachu-as-starter decision was a marketing-driven one rather than a creative-team choice. Producer Mori's bet on Pikachu — partly based on the character's friendliness and cute design, partly based on early plush-toy sales data — became the most consequential anime-marketing decision of the late 1990s. Within two years of the anime's premiere, Pikachu was the most-recognized cartoon character among American children under 10 years old, even ahead of Mickey Mouse for a brief period in 1999.

question: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 4 — Diamond is Unbreakable (1992-1995) — is set in the fictional Japanese town of Morioh in 1999. The arc's antagonist Yoshikage Kira is famously based on a real Japanese serial killer of the late 1990s. Araki cited a specific case while writing the arc; the murderer had a similar quiet-office-worker demeanor and was caught after years of evasion. What real Japanese criminal influenced the Kira character?
answer: Tsutomu Miyazaki, the Tokyo-area 1988-1989 child murderer known as the 'Otaku Murderer'
choices: Tsutomu Miyazaki, the Tokyo-area 1988-1989 child murderer known as the 'Otaku Murderer'
Shoko Asahara, leader of the Aum Shinrikyo cult behind the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack
Akihabara Massacre perpetrator Tomohiro Kato, from a 2008 case that postdated the manga
Hiroshi Maeue, the Internet-suicide-club serial killer of mid-2000s Osaka
context: Araki's research into the Miyazaki case is documented in his author's notes. The 'normal-looking salaryman' aspect of Kira's character design — his desire for a quiet life, his collection of body-part trophies, his methodical evasion — closely mirrors aspects of the Miyazaki case. The Kira character became one of the most-imitated 'banality of evil' antagonist designs in shonen manga. Yoshikage Kira's specific 'I just want a quiet life' speech is among the franchise's most-quoted villain monologues.

question: In Rob Reiner's 1987 The Princess Bride, what phrase does the farm boy Westley say to Buttercup whenever she asks him to do something?
context: Westley's catchphrase is revealed to mean 'I love you.' Cary Elwes played Westley; Robin Wright played Buttercup. William Goldman wrote both the 1973 novel and screenplay.

question: Wallace Shawn's character Vizzini repeatedly exclaims one famous word whenever something happens that he didn't predict in The Princess Bride. What's the word?
context: Inigo Montoya finally responds: 'You keep using that word. I do not think it means what you think it means.' The line became one of the most-quoted in 80s film history.

question: In Scott Pilgrim vs. the World, how many evil exes must Scott defeat to date Ramona Flowers?
context: The League of Evil Exes is led by Gideon Graves, the seventh and final boss. Bryan Lee O'Malley's six graphic novels (2004-2010) inspired Edgar Wright's 2010 film and the 2023 Netflix anime.

question: In the 2023 Super Mario Bros. Movie, what song does Bowser sing on a piano while imprisoned in his airship, declaring his love for Princess Peach?
context: Jack Black voiced Bowser and performed the song, which became a viral hit and was Oscar-shortlisted. The Illumination film was directed by Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic.

question: In 1985's Back to the Future, what kind of car does Doc Brown convert into a time machine?
context: Director Robert Zemeckis chose the DeLorean for its iconic gull-wing doors that would look like a UFO when people first saw it. Christopher Lloyd played Doc Emmett Brown; Michael J. Fox replaced Eric Stoltz as Marty after several weeks of filming.

question: In 1984's Ghostbusters, what's the name of the giant white marshmallow creature that stomps through New York City in the climax?
context: Ray Stantz (Dan Aykroyd) accidentally chose the form by thinking of 'the most harmless thing.' Ivan Reitman directed; the screenplay was by Aykroyd and Harold Ramis.

question: In Doc Brown's lab, Marty McFly's catchphrase reaction to an unbelievable revelation is the same Christopher Lloyd line shouted dozens of times across all three Back to the Future films. What two-word exclamation?
context: Christopher Lloyd ad-libbed the phrasing on set; it appears repeatedly in all three films (1985, 1989, 1990). The 'Doc Brown' character was inspired by physicist Jack Parsons and conductor Leopold Stokowski.

question: In 1984's The Karate Kid, what move does Daniel LaRusso use to win the All-Valley Karate Tournament against Cobra Kai's Johnny Lawrence?
context: Mr. Miyagi (Pat Morita) taught Daniel the crane kick by demonstration on the beach. John G. Avildsen directed; Ralph Macchio played Daniel. The crane kick is technically illegal under tournament rules in the film.

question: In 1986's Top Gun, what's Pete Mitchell's call sign?
context: Tom Cruise played Maverick. Director Tony Scott was Ridley Scott's brother. The Navy got a recruitment boom from the film and reportedly opened recruiting stations near theaters.

question: In 1985's The Goonies, what's the name of the deformed-faced character who joins the kids' treasure hunt and becomes friends with Chunk?
context: John Matuszak played Sloth, the deformed brother of the Fratelli crime family. Director Richard Donner and producer Steven Spielberg developed the story together. Sean Astin played Mikey.

question: In 1982's E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, what brand of candy does Elliott use to lure E.T. into his house?
context: Mars Inc. famously turned down product placement for M&Ms; Hershey paid $1 million for Reese's Pieces. Sales tripled within two weeks of the film's release. Steven Spielberg directed.

question: In 1981's Raiders of the Lost Ark, what relic is Indiana Jones racing the Nazis to find?
context: Steven Spielberg directed; George Lucas produced. Harrison Ford was cast as Indy after Tom Selleck dropped out due to Magnum P.I. commitments. The Ark's opening melts Nazi faces in the climax.

question: In 1984's The Terminator, what catchphrase does Arnold Schwarzenegger's cyborg say to a police-station receptionist before returning with a car to crash through the wall?
context: James Cameron wrote and directed. Schwarzenegger originally objected to the line, suggesting 'I will be back,' but Cameron insisted. The phrase became Arnold's signature.

question: In the Indiana Jones trilogy, what specific piece of clothing is part of Indy's iconic look along with the leather jacket and whip?
context: The hat became so iconic that the production team had a strict 'never lose the hat' rule on set. Harrison Ford wore it across all four films from 1981 to 2008. Originally inspired by old serial-adventure heroes.

question: In 1987's Predator, what does Arnold Schwarzenegger's character shout while urging his team to flee in a helicopter from the Central American jungle?
context: John McTiernan directed. Arnold's character Major Dutch Schaefer leads a special forces team hunting an extraterrestrial big-game hunter. Jesse Ventura plays a teammate; he later became Governor of Minnesota.

question: In 1991's T2, James Cameron's Terminator sequel, what type of advanced cyborg pursues young John Connor and can shape-shift into liquid metal?
context: Robert Patrick played the T-1000. The liquid-metal effects by ILM cost the film much of its $102 million budget — the most expensive film made up to that point. James Cameron returned to direct.
